items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 576-579 (book Lemma 8.1.7): for every point x of the circle and every path p from the base point to x, decoding the encoding of p returns p. The statement is an identity between composites over an arbitrary point, and the proof (source lines 580-587) first uses path induction to reduce it to the reflexivity path at the base point, where the two composites have to be unfolded by definition: encoding reflexivity is transport of the canonical integer along reflexivity, hence zero, and decoding zero is the zeroth power of the generating loop, hence reflexivity. Which definitions have to be unfolded, and why the general case needs no further argument, is the content and the statement shows none of it.
